caveats: `count` is the PRINTED list and stays 73 whatever this file holds; `unprinted` names every record keyed from the body instead of from folios 3-9, and `records = count + len(unprinted)`. `unprinted` means NOT PRINTED IN Authorities Quoted — it is not a claim that the work is unprinted in the book, and no consumer may read it as one. `read_from` is true of the 73 and of nothing else; an unprinted record says in its `note` where it was read from instead.

An unprinted record with `ref: null`, `folio: null`, `printed: []` has no printed block anywhere — jochelson1905, keyed from citations parts 2 and 3 make. An unprinted record that IS printed somewhere in the book keeps its `ref`, `folio` and `printed` block, and the block is the record exactly as it is for the 73. The nulls used to be forced on every unprinted record by the span gate, which ran in both directions and failed any entry naming a leaf outside the `authorities` run; `edition runs` now checks one way only (a run demands every leaf it names be witnessed, the store may hold more), so a record no longer has to discard the leaf it is printed on in order to be admitted. Such a record still renders on no leaf: apparatus.entries_for resolves the leaf to a run first, and no run covers it.

The chapter XXIII footnote on 3-146/3-147 (folios 680-681) is a SECOND printed bibliography: twenty-one numbered works, most set twice as the front list is, opening 'Besides the sources enumerated in the list of authorities (p. 3)' and closing with the very sentence folio 9 closes with. It is what the folio-9 asterism points at. Those leaves are ordinary text pages (gt/zones _train.lst), not apparatus leaves, so their content reaches the edition through gt/ocr -> TEI; a run over them would render the bibliography twice, which is why there is no second run and why these records carry ref without one. All twenty-one are here, items 1-17 on 3-146 and 18-21 on 3-147, and the run page shows them under their own heading after the printed list rather than inside it.

MINTING A RECORD AND IDENTIFYING A WORK ARE TWO ACTS, and only the second needs an external witness. `printed` is the record, so a record built from a keyed printed block asserts nothing beyond what the page sets and needs no lookup at all. Matching an entry to a published work is enrichment and lives in `note`, `doi` and `url`, every one of them #llm until a human opens the link. Twenty of the twenty-one now carry an identification, four made while keying (acts1841, holyfathers1850, anon1790, priklonsky1896) and sixteen in a later pass against library catalogues; every one of them is #llm and unratified, and eight carry a located scan in `url`, also #llm. The twenty-first, anon1856, says the identification was SEARCHED AND NOT FOUND, and that sentence is the honest state, not a placeholder to be filled by guessing — the same rule that governed `Identification not looked up` before it. Two of the sixteen changed how a printed fact reads and say so in their own notes: baramygin1855's bare `57` is a publication year, not a volume, and its 1855 is the year of the journey; pilgrim1887's English `(monthly)` is wrong about a weekly, which is why the two witnesses are kept apart rather than merged. One near-miss was caught and is recorded rather than filed: muller1750's title resolves to an 1787 second edition on prlib.

Four keys in the 3-146/3-147 batch carry NO year — supplements, monuments, senatearchive and (in the front list's own style) any future one like them — because their entries print none. The house key form is name+year; inventing a year to satisfy it would put a fabricated fact in the one field a reader most expects to be witnessed, so the stem stands alone instead. baramygin1855 is the opposite case and is flagged in its own note: its year comes from the English witness only, the Russian block printing no date.

The list is explicitly OPEN. The section closes on folio 9 with an asterism and the line recorded in closing_note, so a citation in the body with no entry here is expected and is not a reconciliation failure. This is unlike data/loi.json, where a figure outside 1-302 is a defect.

`printed` is the record. The parsed fields (author, title, title_en, year, place, container) are a derived convenience and may flatten what the block actually says; when they disagree with `printed`, `printed` wins.

Russian entries are in pre-1918 orthography. The letters ъ ѣ і ѳ and endings -аго/-яго are NOT misspellings and must never be 'corrected'. The collation licence to fix European-language orthography does not reach them.

Most entries in Russian are printed twice: the original, then Bogoras's own English rendering in square brackets. One work, two `printed` blocks, kind `entry` and kind `translation`. The brackets are retained in the text.

A repeated author is printed as a long rule, not a name. The rule is not reproduced in `text`; its presence is recorded as author_printed: "rule", and `author` carries the inherited name. Where the block opens '[———— Title', the bracket is kept and the rule dropped.

cited_as is the load-bearing field: it is the only witness to what a body-text short citation resolves to. It is structured (name, volume, short_title) rather than a string, because the surface form in the body is NOT the form printed here and a string would bake in typography that the text does not reproduce.

The small caps are this page's setting only, and are deliberately NOT carried into cited_as. In the body the citation is set upper-and-lower: the footnote reads 'Dall, I, p. 375.' where the entry prints 'DALL, I'. cited_as.name holds the upper-and-lower form; match it case-insensitively anyway.

Punctuation before the volume numeral is inconsistent in the body — 'Maydell I, p. 331.' against 'Krasheninnikoff, II, p. 49.' — so the comma cannot be relied on to delimit the volume. This is why volume is its own field.

A siglum printed over several volumes (Krasheninnikoff, Maydell, Slunin, Nordenskiöld — each set as 'NAME, I, II') is split into one cited_as entry per volume, since the body cites them singly. 47 printed sigla, 51 cited_as entries.

Most references in the body are not sigla at all. They are indirect prose — 'Krause reports that…' — where only the name appears, with no volume, no short title, and no footnote. A resolver keyed solely on the footnote form will miss the majority of citations; cited_as.name is the field that reaches them, and it is ambiguous by construction where two works share a name (Hooper, Krause, Adler, Jackson, Kyber, Dall, Argentoff, Mason, Hough, Boas, Bogoras, Murdoch, Jochelson, Maydell, Neimann, Sarytcheff, Wrangell).
Ordering follows the print and is roughly but not strictly chronological (maydell1871 is set among the 1893 entries, murdoch1884 after murdoch1888). Do not sort by year and call it the printed order.

Curly quotation marks and apostrophes reproduce the print, per the corpus rule. The exact form of the closing mark on the Russian quoted title in melikoff1896 is not resolvable at this magnification; see that record's note.
doi and url are null throughout: no external identifier has been looked up yet. These are the enrichment slots.

`provenance` on a doi or url is #llm where a model proposed the match and #ed where a human supplied or opened the link. Every #llm one is unratified by construction; jochelson1905's url is the first #ed, handed over by the editor.

IDENTIFIED, and the identification changes how two printed facts read: the work is `Путевой журналъ купца Михаила Барамыгина, во время поѣздки изъ Нижнеколымска въ Анюйскую крѣпость въ 1855 году`, communicated by Sverbeyev, in `Записки Сибирскаго отдѣла Императорскаго Русскаго Географическаго Общества`, кн. IV, 1857. First, the 1855 the English witness alone supplies is corroborated — but as the year of the JOURNEY, which the work's own title carries, not of publication; the record's `year` and this key therefore hold a travel date, and no consumer may read them as an imprint date. Second, the bare `57` both witnesses set is that publication year abbreviated, not a volume number: кн. 4 is the volume and the Записки Сибирскаго отдѣла never ran to a vol. 57. The reading stands as printed either way. Identification #llm, from two bibliographic indexes and no copy seen; unratified.
